Chestnut Springs #2

Heartless

Elsie Silver, Cristina Stan (Translator)

4.35
659,633 ratings65,185 reviews
Rate this book
Să lucrez ca bonă pentru un tată singur, distant și foarte serios nu ar trebui să fie greu. Problema e că nu pot să-mi iau ochii de la el. Iar el nu poate sta departe de mine.

În vara asta am un job nou, la ferma Fântâna Dorințelor: să fiu bona lui Luke, băiețelul lui Cade Eaton.

Cade este cu treisprezece ani mai mare decât mine și abia dacă-mi aruncă vreo privire. Dar când îl prind la înghesuială în jacuzzi și jucăm „adevăr sau provocare”, pare că totul devine posibil. Poate că hainele vor zbura de pe noi imediat…

Cade e un tip cam din topor. Cu toate acestea, am descoperit repede că eu, orășeancă get-beget, am o slăbiciune: bărbații bine-făcuți și slobozi la gură.

Când suntem doar noi doi, Cade se poartă mai blând. Încep să bănuiesc că duritatea pe care o afișează mereu este doar de dragul aparențelor. Odată, cineva i-a băgat în cap ideea că, oricât de mult se va strădui, niciodată nu va fi de ajuns.

Însă, atunci când Cade mă ține în brațe, mă simt mai prețuită ca niciodată.

M-am învoit să am grijă de Luke.

Am încheiat o înțelegere doar pentru două luni…

Dar inima îmi spune că voi rămâne pentru totdeauna.

„Proza lui Elsie Silver este o adevărată revelație!”

Ali Hazelwood, autoarea bestsellerului Ipoteza iubirii

About the author

Elsie Silver

27 books82.4k followers
Elsie Silver is a #1 New York Times bestselling author of sassy, steamy, small town romance. She’s a born and raised Canadian girl who loves a good book boyfriend and the strong heroines who bring them to their knees. Her books promise banter, tension, and a slow burn that comes to a screeching halt.

CONCLUSION

Heartless has only proven once again why the single-parent trope is and will always be a smash for me. That trope has never disappointed me so far. I didn’t like the first book in this series that much, but after knowing the trope of Heartless and getting to know Cade and Willa a bit in Flawless and seeing how they were complete opposite and I KNEW they were going to be my favorite couple in this series.

Comment to add after just finishing the bonus epilogue for Heartless: omg I love Cade, Willa, Emma and Luke all so much. my family, my heart. why are they so wholesome. Everybody go read this book now! 😩

I am obsessed with this book. I got lost in this book. There is nothing heartless about Cade Eaton. I mean, come on: "You want it all, Willa? The house? The babies? The ranch?" YES CADE SHE DOES. WE ALL DO. 🤠🖤🐮👨‍👩‍👦🦖🧑🏽‍🌾🌶️🥵

Cade and Willa's story is best described by Summer as follows: "It's two people who were both a little lost until they ended up on the same path and walked together for a while."

Ok, so. Basically next to the dictionary definition of "cowboy" there is just a picture of Cade Eaton. That's it. He is the literal ideal cowboy that you picture reading a western. He's also unproblematic. Drama free. DOESN'T F*CK ANYTHING UP with Willa! Just so solid and sturdy, though at first to a fault. Anyways, I don't even usually like books with the single-dad trope or the nanny trope. But this book??? Maybe it's just Cade and his batman-cowboy persona, or maybe its just how well-written this story is. It doesn't feel like you're reading some cheesy story about a dad and a nanny. Its deeper than that, more realistic. Willa is this fiery, free-spirited redhead who is sort of lost and doesn't know what she wants from life yet. She's never nannied or babysat in her life but agrees to help watch Cade's son Luke (who is simply the sweetest funniest little man ever) for the summer to pass the time. Cade is big and broody and jaded, hardheaded, stubborn, stuck in his ways, doesn't trust others and doesn't smile. Enter our spunky Willa girl and expect both of their worlds to catch on fire.

Think: spiiicy slow burn, him trying to pretend he's not falling for her, her hella flirting and teasing and generally driving him crazy, the sweetest moments between little Luke and Willa, the slow domestication of firey Willa and the undoing of strict Cade, sexy hot tub nights with truth or dare, rodeo events, slow dancing in the kitchen, a possessive and caretaking cowboy daddy, and fun cameos from Summer and the Eaton boys.

Flying through this series. I loooved this even more than the first one. I thought the spice was much better (something about Willa and Cade just felt really authentic and raw), the bantering was even more perfect, and if I hadn't already fallen in love with Chestnut Springs and Wishing Well Ranch I am now totally a goner. This book was so sweet and lovely. I don't necessarily need another book about Rhett and Summer, but I'd do terrible things for a sequel where we see more of just Luke and Willa and Cade living their happy ever after together. Hoping to get a little of that in the next two books. Anyways, Elsie Silver is SUCH a good writer and this book had zero flaws.

I am definitely in my cowboy era and don't plan on leaving anytime soon. Well, at least until I finish this series. Chestnut Srings should be a real place because I want to go visit now.

Heartless is the second book in the Chestnut Springs series, and ya'll, it did not disappoint. This small town, age gap, single dad/nanny, cowboy romance hit the spot with its banter, sexual tension, and humor. This had me giggling and kicking my feet throughout. It has now easily become my favorite in the series so far.

Cade is a rancher who will be busy for the summer and is in need of a nanny for his son Luke. He has turned down all of the applicants as he didn't like them and is now desperate. When Summer suggests her friend Willa that has come to visit. Now, seeing that Willa is the woman that he had an awkward meet cute with at the local coffee shop earlier that day, but what other options does he have. It's when he sees Willa interact with his son that he decides to give her a chance.


Cade Eaton damn this man is a grumpy, protective, broken selfles caretaker that indeed is so much daddy. The man who is always responsible and serious has a dirty dirty mouth that I was eating up. The way that he is so soft and sweet with his son and Willa and helping her with overcoming her insecurities in the sweetest of ways had me in a swoon worthy trance.

“Thank you. Thank you for being the first person in my life to put me first, to give me options. I’m not sure I deserve that gift, but I know that I’ll never forget it for as long as I live.”


Willa Grant is a breath of fresh air with her sunshine, strong, sassy, and fiesty personality. She had some insecurites but didn't let them define the badass that she is. I love that she tells it like it is and gives herself pep talks when she feels uncomfortable. One of the best things that she did was push a kid into a pool for picking on Luke. This had me downright laughing so hard.

“Beg.” “Pardon me?” “You heard me.” Her lips don’t even twitch. She’s not joking at all. “Beg.”


Luke Eaton I absolutely loved and adored this kid so much. He kept things light and had me cracking up at some of the things that came out of his mouth. It was definitely never a dull moment when he was around. The relationship that him and Willa had was heartwarming to witness.

“Hey, Willa?”“Hey, Luke,” I reply dryly, since the be quiet part obviously didn’t register. “Sometimes I wish you were my mom.”


Cade and Willa their relationship blossomed slowly from their push and pull from each other to chemistry that was undeniably palpable. They were the definition of opposites but fit so well together. Some of their moments were straight fire.

“You want it all, Willa? The house? The babies? The ranch?” I nod again because it’s all I can do. I want all that. With him. “You want me, Willa?”“Yes.” I cry out against the soft fabric, nodding frantically as he slams into me. I want him so badly it hurts. “Good. Because I’m sick of holding back with you. You’re not going anywhere. You belong here, with me.”


I found myself not being able to put this book down. It had me wanting more with every turn of the page. I also enjoyed Summer and Rhett so much more in this than their book. They had the best group text that I wanted so badly to join in on. The ending was just so sweet and wholesome. It makes me want to be a part of this big family.

Pre-review: It's time for the grumpy single dad cowboy, Cade 🤠 and to find out if he really is daddy 🤭🤭
Ri ♡
605 reviews2,290 followers
June 26, 2023
4.75 stars

“I realize in that moment maybe I am heartless after all, because the beautiful girl with the copper hair grinning back at me right now is the one who stole it.”


I’m officially and wholeheartedly in my country-boy era because they just do it better than any other fictional men. What the hell kind of crack did Elsie put in this book that made me devour it in just two days?! This was the funniest, swooniest, and sweetest book—so adorable. I’m so in love with Cade, Willa, and Luke and their sweet little wholesome family.

Heartless is my comfort book, and I can read it over and over again. I loved the story so much, and it’s adorable because of Willa and Luke’s precious, chaotic moments. And it’s sexy because Willa and Cade are fire. The pacing was a little slow in this one, but the whole storyline was constructed perfectly from the start to the most endearing ending. Even though the nanny and single-dad trope is such a typical plot in the small-town romance genre, Willa and Cade made everything about this book perfect with their top-notch banter and scorching chemistry.

I quirk a brow in her direction. “You know the rule, Red?”
“You wear the hat, you ride the cowboy.” She winks at me, looking fucking adorable wearing my hat.


Willa Grant is fire. If attitude were a person, she’d be it. A bartender turned nanny for a hot single dad who’s also a rancher. She’s carefree, funny, loyal, and has a witty sense of humour with a very sassy mouth. She’s such a badass but also a little insecure about her future and herself. This girl is a firecracker, a hurricane who melted all the walls Cade built around himself as protection—just by earning his trust. And she’s the girl who pushed a kid in the pool because he bullied Luke. I wanna be badass Willa Grant so badly right now. I loved her from the very first chapter, and the urge to leave everything behind and be Willa Grant is so strong right now.

“Willa might be a bit of psycho—after all, she did just push a child into the pool—but the more time I spend with her, the more I feel like she’s my psycho.”


Cade Eaton is a hot cowboy, a rancher, and a single dad to the most adorable kid. He’s grumpy and a little infuriating—he doesn’t know how to make jokes or even communicate sometimes—but he’s the most thoughtful, selfless, and caring person I have ever seen. His actions speak louder than his words, and the things he did for his family as the oldest child, as a single dad to Luke, and as the most amazing person Willa needed—were everything. And we all know he’s also known for his dirty, dirty mouth, which is a threat to my ovaries.

“Daddy Cade, you’re a whole lot prettier when you smile.”


Cade Eaton’s dirty mouth and Willa Grant’s sassy mouth are the most dangerous combination in this world. Cade and Willa are opposites in every way. While Willa is fire, Cade is ice—but the moment they met, there was always this undeniable electric chemistry and connection between them. No matter how much he tried to push her away or tried to hate chaotic Willa, he was always drawn to her. And she’s the only one who thawed his icy heart. They complement each other so well that I can never imagine one without the other. From their first meeting—when she dropped her panties—to the moment she asked him to beg her to stay, everything about them was epic. Their forced proximity, the slow burn, the push-and-pull relationship made the sexual tension between them palpable, and that hot tub scene was chef’s kiss. They both knew what they wanted, and they took it however they wanted. They are mother and father for real.

“What are you doing?” I grumble as I wipe at my watery eyes, no doubt smudged with mascara.
“Taking care of you,” he replies without even looking my way. His tone says that I just asked him a stupid question.
“That’s fine. I can take care of myself.”
“I know you can, but you don’t have to because I’m here to help.”


The way they both cared for each other and tried to be there for each other when needed—it was beautiful. Cade had trust issues because of his ex-wife, but Willa proved to him that she was the one he needed. She’s his comfort person and his little troublemaker. Willa was insecure about herself, but Cade made her feel like she was the most amazing, perfect person—that she could be anyone she wanted, and he’d still love her. He’d leave all the post-it notes for her forever. They are so perfect and everything, I love them so much.

“You want it all, Willa? The house? The babies? The ranch?”
I nod again because it’s all I can do. I want all that. With him.
“You want me, Willa?”
“Yes.”
“Good. Because I’m sick of holding back with you. You’re not going anywhere. You belong here, with me.”


Luke Eaton is the most adorable, funny, and goofy kid. Always running around and doing chaotic things. I freaking adore this boy so much, and he deserves the best—he deserves Willa and all the happiness in this world. I’m glad he has Willa, who loves him more than anything.

“Did you know I fell in love with you before I fell in love with your dad?”
His eyes light at that. “You did?”
I nod, pulling him close with an arm around his shoulders. “I did.”


THE BEST THING IN THIS BOOK WAS THE FAMILY DYNAMICS. It was beautiful to see Willa slowly but surely become a part of Cade and Luke’s small world. Willa and Luke were perfect, and I wanna protect them and never let them go. The way she treated Luke was so, so endearing. And I support Willa throwing bully kids in the pool. She understood that kid and his father and gave them the love, comfort, and family they deserved. They are all so precious.

“I’d do it for everything she’s given me in such a short time . . .
A love Luke has never known.
A reason for me to smile again.
A person to talk to after so many years of silence.
A love I’ve never known.”


Heartless and Reckless are my absolute favourites in this series because Cade Eaton and Theo Silva supremacy. I love this series with all my heart. The ending was perfect, with a very cute little surprise. There was a little drama at the end, but it wasn’t stretched for chapters and chapters—everything was perfect. I’m so happy for Cade, Willa, and their sweet, wholesome, adorable family.

5 stars



I’ve read most of Elsie Silver’s books and I’ve enjoyed them all but THIS is the book! This one is by far my favorite book of hers and I’m positive it will be on my favorites list this year! Heartless had so much I love in a book. Single dad… check. Grumpy hero… check. Forced proximity… check. Age gap… check! I swear it’s like she wrote this one just for me!

Cade Eaton is in need of a nanny for his son, Luke, while he works on/runs the family farm all summer. He can’t find anyone so Summer has her best friend, Willa come to town and work the job for the summer. Cade is not excited about this. Willa is young, thirteen years younger than his 38 and does she even have experience with kids? Since Summer vouches for her, he gives her a chance but he is unsure.

Willa doesn’t have much experience with kids, but being with Luke all day and playing is too easy and fun. Their relationship (Luke and Willa) is completely heartwarming. I smiled so much seeing those two together. Seeing Luke and Willa together makes Cade come around a little quicker too.

Cade was burned by a woman and he’s just here to focus on his kid, work, and family. He doesn’t want a relationship but there is just something about Willa. A grumpy hero who is soft with his son and starts to thaw for his nanny… seriously you just can’t go wrong with this book. The sweetest scenes, the family stuff that I adored, and the steam was top notch. I love Elsie Silver’s writing style and she killed it with this book.

This series is shaping up to be fantastic. I loved Rhett’s book, I loved Cade’s book, and soon enough (hopefully) we’ll get Jasper and Beau’s books and I couldn’t be more excited. I’m loving being in the ‘Chestnut Springs’ world and I never want to leave. Heartless was truly perfect for me- there wasn’t a thing I didn’t love. I’ll be recommending this one to everyone!

4.5 stars

Willa & Cade were exceptionally the best and the soft moments besides the sexual innuendos/ witty banter between them delivered a pleasant and fun time (it’s safe to say they’ve won me over).

Willa felt like such a reprieve from other fmcs with her personality in being strong willed + loving with a spine and her unhinged sense of humor made it impossible not to love her!! She was soft and fierce to her core and her pep talks when stressed were sending me (she’s very much my spirit animal). Bonus points for pushing that kid into the pool. I reveled in her ability to be so blunt in saying what’s on her mind, putting anyone in their place and just who she is as a person that I was able to connect to. My petition to be included in the group chat is quite embarrassing but we’d be such good friends haha

Now Cade.. the best grump yet such a charmer and so soft with Willa. The fact that he was communicative and supportive of Willa knowing how she is and what she needed had my support and vice versa. This man had such a filthy mouth and knew how to use it. I mean, you know that famous quote “save a horse, ride a cowboy?” Yeah, It was meant for him 🤠 now the build up to their relationship felt entirely entrancing & the tension here fueled me that I felt like I was drowning in it. This book was mostly all humor, horny moments paired with some soft moments to which worked for me. Anyways, certain scenes left plenty to the imagination and all I’ll say is daddy cade indeed lmao I think he’s my favorite Eaton brother without reading beau’s book and don’t ask me how I know—I just know it

As for Luke, I absolutely adored this kid and his relationship with Willa 🥹 their scenes warmed my heart and I loved how protective she was of him. Also, I quite liked Rhett and summer here and the text threads with everyone >> I know there’s bonus POVs for Harvey but I still think he needs his own novella

I saw this as more than a “cowboy romance” given certain factors in the storyline with the characters internal fears— in particular Cades complex background and their mutual understanding of the needs of one another. It all ultimately by the end made this feel a little deeper which i liked and it was overall such an enjoyable time and i loved it. Down the rabbit hole i go now for more books like this so *consider that your sign to read this*

heartless by elsie silver was such a great story! i thought that this would be underwhelming, but oh boy, was i wrong!

౨ৎ willa. this woman was made to be a mom even without really the experience of handling kids. some people are just really meant to be parents even without them knowing. i love her loyalty, and the way it was showed throughout the book. the way she stood up for the people that means a lot to her, even if they’re present or not, is truly admirable. once you earn her trust, she’d truly always have your back. moreover, i feel like her struggle as a kid who wasn’t pressured by her parents is often overlooked, but i truly think that putting a little bit of pressure on kids really gives them the direction they need. it shows that anything too much or too little is bad.

౨ৎ cade. this man is such a daddy, and i mean that both literally and you definitely know the other one i’m talking about. everything about this man is so hot, and i’m not even kidding! i truly can’t imagine how hard it was for him to be the dad of his brothers and sister when his mom died, but i know for sure that it made him think that it’s just his role, which isn’t the case because he deserves to put himself first before others, and i’m glad willa showed him that.

overall, this book was sooo good! i swear i wasn’t expecting much because again, the first book ended up being underwhelming for me, but this book exceeded my expectations! i'd definitely recommend this book to anyone who loves to read about a single dad who lives in a small town + they're grumpy but it just really makes him hotter!
